title: Introduce timeline-based sensitivity reporter and noisy-prompt bloom filter CI hook
author: Diego Alvarez
release_notes: Adds a timeline sensitivity reporter and a non-blocking CI hook that reduces false-positive regressions using a noisy-prompt bloom filter. No public API changes.
description:
Motivation: We repeatedly see short-lived spikes in per-prompt regression signals that trigger noisy CI failures or noisy alerts. This PR introduces a timeline-based sensitivity reporter that aggregates per-prompt metric deltas over sliding time windows and applies robust smoothing + outlier suppression so transient blips do not immediately escalate.

Design summary: The reporter computes a per-prompt sensitivity series (delta in metric vs baseline) on each eval run and maintains a short-term timeline of snapshots (default 7 recent evaluations spanning multiple CI runs). The series is processed with an EMA (alpha configurable) followed by a Hampel-style outlier detector to identify single-point spikes. Prompts flagged as "noisy" are tracked in a per-window Bloom filter so the CI hook can suppress gating for prompts that have historically shown intermittent volatility. The CI hook is non-blocking by default and emits advisory regression tickets; teams can opt-in to fail-on-regressions via a label or per-linear policy.

Implementation: - New module eval_harness.reporting.timeline_sensitivity.py: implements timeline state, EMA smoothing, Hampel detector, and Bloom filter windowing (4 hash functions, 1024-bit per-window by default). - CI adapter eval_harness.ci.timeline_hook: wraps existing smoke-eval runner, merges timeline snapshots from the run artifacts, and posts a structured advisory to the CI UI. - Persistence: timeline snapshots stored as small JSON blobs in the existing artifacts bucket under artifacts/eval/timeline/ to avoid introducing a new DB. - Config: feature toggles + thresholds via eval-config.yaml (new section 'timeline_sensitivity').

Testing and validation: added unit tests for smoothing/outlier logic and Bloom filter ops; added an integration smoke test that replays three synthetic eval runs to validate suppression behavior. Locally ran the end-to-end smoke suite and a short perf benchmark.

Rollout plan: feature behind config flag off by default. Ship as advisory for 2 weeks, monitor advisory-to-action ratio. Post-rollout, we will expose an opt-in gating mode for teams that want automatic quarantine of severe regressions.

Notes: This is intentionally non-invasive: no changes to existing metric schemas, downstream dashboards, or alerting. Intended to reduce noise in CI/regression pipelines and speed triage.
